reference.source: Stiehm's Immunologic Disorders / IUIS classification of inborn errors of immunity
clinicalPearls: Presents with recurrent sinopulmonary bacterial infection often complicated by early bronchiectasis, alongside a marked tendency to persistent or severe herpesvirus infection such as EBV and CMV
Non-malignant lymphoproliferation is characteristic, with generalised lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly and mucosal lymphoid hyperplasia
APDS1 arises from gain-of-function variants in PIK3CD (p110-delta) and APDS2 from loss-of-function variants in the regulatory subunit gene PIK3R1, both increasing PI3K-delta signalling
The immunophenotype shows an excess of senescent, terminally differentiated effector T cells with reduced naive T cells and progressive CD4 lymphopenia
Antibody responses are impaired with dysregulated immunoglobulins, often raised IgM with low IgG, so immunoglobulin replacement is frequently required
There is a substantially increased risk of B-cell lymphoma, driven in part by persistent EBV infection
Inheritance is autosomal dominant and the phenotype is highly variable even within families
Targeted therapy with selective PI3K-delta inhibitors or with sirolimus can reduce lymphoproliferation, and haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is considered in severe disease
reference.pathophysiology: APDS results from constitutive over-activity of the phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta pathway, either through activating variants in the catalytic subunit p110-delta (PIK3CD) or loss of the inhibitory regulatory subunit p85-alpha (PIK3R1). Excessive signalling through the downstream AKT-mTOR axis drives inappropriate lymphocyte activation and proliferation while promoting premature differentiation and senescence of effector T cells and impairing the generation and survival of naive and memory populations. Defective B-cell maturation and class switching produce a dysregulated antibody response, and the combination of impaired viral control and persistent lymphoproliferation underlies the recurrent infections, EBV-associated disease and lymphoma risk.
additionalInvestigations: Lymphocyte subsets showing reduced naive T cells with expanded senescent effector T cells and skewed B-cell maturation
Serum immunoglobulins, often with elevated IgM and reduced IgG, and specific antibody responses
Assessment of PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway activity where available
EBV and CMV viral load monitoring
Targeted sequencing of PIK3CD and PIK3R1 for characteristic gain-of-function or splice variants
High-resolution chest imaging for bronchiectasis and imaging of lymphoid organs
redFlags: Rapidly enlarging or asymmetric lymphadenopathy suggesting lymphoma
Rising EBV viral load with systemic symptoms
Refractory cytopenias or organomegaly causing functional compromise
reference.prognosis: Outcome varies widely; recurrent infection and bronchiectasis cause chronic morbidity while lymphoma is a major cause of death, but selective PI3K-delta inhibition and, in selected patients, transplantation have improved disease control.
pitfalls: Labelling the condition common variable immunodeficiency and missing the specific targetable pathway defect
Mistaking benign lymphoproliferation for lymphoma or vice versa without histology
Overlooking early bronchiectasis because chest examination and spirometry appear normal
Failing to monitor and pre-emptively manage EBV
Using broad immunosuppression without recognising the option of pathway-specific therapy
references: Stiehm's Immunologic Disorders in Infants and Children
IUIS Expert Committee classification of inborn errors of immunity
management: Targeted selective PI3K-delta inhibition with leniolisib as disease-specific therapy, with mTOR inhibition using sirolimus as an alternative for lymphoproliferation
Immunoglobulin replacement therapy for the dysregulated antibody response and impaired IgG
Antimicrobial prophylaxis with prompt treatment of bacterial infection, and antiviral therapy for EBV and CMV disease
Airway clearance physiotherapy and aggressive treatment of exacerbations to manage bronchiectasis
Surveillance for B-cell lymphoma with monitoring of EBV and CMV viral loads and lymphoid-organ imaging
Haematopoietic stem cell transplantation in selected severe or transformation-prone cases
Coordinated multidisciplinary clinical immunology and haematology-oncology care, with genetic counselling for the autosomal dominant PIK3CD or PIK3R1 variant and family testing
